title: MongoDB connection from the Allocations Handler is unauthenticated and unencrypted on the container network
notes: Conditional on an attacker reaching the internal Compose network. The default configuration supports the unauthenticated/unencrypted MongoDB connection claim, but the threat cites no evidence items.

title: Unvalidated threshold query value flows into the allocations MongoDB lookup
notes: Threshold injection is real through string interpolation into $where, but the example threshold[$gt]= would not work as described (it interpolates as [object Object]). ev-route-14 correctly locates the affected route; it does not itself show the vulnerable DAO line.

title: Unbounded allocations query from the handler can be used to exhaust database resources
notes: The unbounded query and repeated per-allocation user lookups support a conditional resource-exhaustion threat, but actual database saturation depends on request volume, data size, and external rate controls. ev-route-14 correctly locates the route but does not prove the missing controls.

title: No per-request audit trail for cross-user allocation reads
notes: The pinned application code has no per-request audit trail tying allocation reads to the authenticated account. External logging remains an assumption. ev-gap-1 supports the cross-user access precondition, but not the missing-audit-trail claim.

title: IDOR on GET /allocations/:userId exposes other users' allocation records
Credentials and session cookie on the allocations request can be read on the wire if the app is served over plain HTTP
notes: Explicitly depends on direct plain-HTTP deployment without TLS termination. In that setting, the session cookie can be intercepted and replayed. GET /allocations carries a session cookie, not login credentials, so the title overstates that part. No cited evidence items.

title: Insecure direct object reference on GET /allocations/:userId exposes other employees' allocations
Unvalidated threshold query parameter reaches the allocations Mongo query
notes: Duplicates threat-2 on the browser-to-handler flow. The pinned DAO confirms raw threshold interpolation into $where. ev-route-14 correctly locates the affected route but does not directly show the DAO flaw.

title: Session cookie forgery and hijacking because the session/auth check trusts an unprotected req.session.userId
notes: Cookie capture and replay are supported only for a deployment without TLS termination. The missing Secure flag and default connect.sid name overlap the bundled session-cookie item. The title's forgery claim is not established: req.session.userId is server-side state. ev-route-7 correctly locates the dashboard request but does not prove the transport or cookie configuration.

title: Session fixation and forged state via the in-process auth check with CSRF protection disabled
notes: The scenario describes CSRF against POST /contributions or POST /profile, and the pinned application has no CSRF check. Cross-site cookie behavior (SameSite defaults) can affect exploitability. The title also says session fixation, but the scenario does not establish that attack, so NG-SESSION-FIXATION is not matched. ev-route-7 locates GET /dashboard, not either state-changing route in the claim.

title: Unbounded session-checked request handling lets a single client stall the Node process
notes: The application has no rate limiter and these routes perform database work per request, so resource exhaustion is plausible under sufficient traffic. Actual process or database saturation depends on traffic volume, capacity, and external controls. ev-route-7 correctly locates /dashboard, one of the named routes, but does not prove the missing limit. The MongoDB authentication assumption is irrelevant to this request-volume claim.

title: Unvalidated redirect on GET /learn sends users to an attacker-controlled login page
notes: GET /learn directly redirects to req.query.url, so the open-redirect claim is supported and duplicates threats 52 and 54. ev-gap-2 says the file imports no validation library, which does not establish the absence of a redirect allow-list. The threat is attached to an unrelated rendering flow, but its scenario names the correct route.

title: Missing security response headers on rendered Swig pages allow clickjacking and unrestricted script sources
notes: ERRATUM 2026-09-25: was supported=y in the original labels (baseline hash unchanged). Clickjacking needs the framed page to be logged in, but connect.sid has no SameSite attribute (express-session 1.15.6: "Path=/; HttpOnly"), so Chrome's Lax default, Firefox Total Cookie Protection and Safari third-party blocking all leave a cross-site iframe logged out. The script-src half assumes an injection it never establishes. Original note: The pinned code leaves Helmet's frameguard and CSP disabled, subject to headers a deployment proxy might add. A logged-in clickjacking example depends on cross-site iframe cookie behavior. Missing CSP removes a defense but does not itself load attacker script; that needs an injection path. The CSRF assumption is not needed for the missing-headers finding. No cited evidence items.

title: Unencrypted HTTP delivery of rendered pages exposes the session cookie and profile data
notes: Explicitly depends on deployment without TLS termination. In that setting, /profile exposes rendered SSN and bank details on the wire, and the session cookie can be captured and replayed. The missing HSTS setting is not the cause of plaintext transport. Duplicates the deployment-dependent HTTP issue in threats 6 and 9. No cited evidence items.

title: Another user's allocations rendered back to any logged-in caller via GET /allocations/:userId
notes: The pinned route and handler support cross-user allocation reads, and ev-gap-1 directly identifies the missing ownership check. Duplicates threats 5 and 7. MongoDB authentication is irrelevant to this application-level IDOR, and the rendering-flow attachment does not change the claim.

title: Swig 1.4.2 arbitrary local file read through template rendering
notes: The lockfile installs Swig 1.4.2, which the advisory lists as affected, but the pinned application uses fixed template names and does not let request data control include or extends directives. The stated attack precondition is not met, so ev-osv-8 does not support this NodeGoat file-read scenario. package.json declares a range; the lockfile pins the installed version.

title: Unauthenticated MongoDB on the benefits-handler to nodegoat flow exposes the whole users collection
notes: Duplicates threat-1 on the benefits-to-MongoDB flow. The default Compose configuration supports an unauthenticated, unencrypted connection to the users collection, conditional on attacker access to the internal network. An anonymous client does not need to impersonate the Benefits Handler. No cited evidence items.

title: Unbounded roster read on the benefits flow can be used to exhaust the application
notes: The benefits DAO loads the full non-admin roster without a limit on GET /benefits and after POST /benefits. Repeated requests could exhaust resources, though saturation depends on traffic volume, collection size, and external controls. Both route citations correctly locate the named paths but do not prove the unbounded query. This is a resource-exhaustion finding, not a match for NG-MISSING-FUNCTION-AUTHZ.
